examples.en: Many guests attended today's event.
The host introduces the guests one by one.
We prepared separate seats for the guests in the front row.

examples.ko: 졸업식에 내빈으로 오신 분이 축사를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: A person who came as a guest to the graduation gave a congratulatory speech.
We prepared gifts for the guests.

examples.ko: 내빈께서 도착하시기 전에 의자를 정리해 주세요.
examples.en: Please arrange the chairs before the guests arrive.

explain: 입학식, 졸업식, 개업식 같은 행사에 초대받아 온 손님을 말해요. 평소 집에 오는 손님은 '손님'이라고 하고, '내빈'은 행사 안내나 사회자 말에서 주로 들려요. 격식 있는 자리에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to invited guests at events such as entrance ceremonies, graduations and openings. A visitor to your home is just '손님'; '내빈' is mostly heard in event announcements and from hosts. It belongs to formal occasions.

examples.en: He lightened the mood with some playful chatter.

examples.ko: 너스레 좀 그만 떨고 본론을 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Stop the empty chatter and get to the point.
Everyone burst out laughing at my friend's patter.

examples.ko: 너스레가 좋아서 손님들이 그 가게를 좋아해요.
examples.en: Because his patter is so good, customers like that shop.
The boss livens up the shop with his jokey talk.
It was awkward, so I tried joking around, but it was no use.

explain: 거짓말이나 과장을 섞어 능청스럽게 늘어놓는 말이에요. 보통 '너스레를 떨다'나 '너스레를 놓다'로 쓰고, 나쁜 뜻만 있는 건 아니라서 어색한 분위기를 풀려는 농담에도 써요.
explain_en: It means glib, somewhat exaggerated talk delivered with a straight face. It is usually used as '너스레를 떨다' or '너스레를 놓다', and it is not purely negative, since it can also describe jokes meant to ease an awkward mood.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 입담이 좋아서 어디서나 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That friend has the gift of gab, so he's popular everywhere.

examples.ko: 선생님의 입담 덕분에 수업이 지루하지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the teacher's way with words, class is never boring.

examples.ko: 입담 좋은 사회자가 분위기를 띄워 줬어요.
examples.en: A host with a silver tongue livened up the mood.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 구수한 입담에 아이들이 웃음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The children burst out laughing at Grandpa's warm storytelling.

examples.ko: 라디오 진행자의 걸쭉한 입담을 들으려고 매일 들어요.
examples.en: I listen every day to hear the radio host's salty, entertaining talk.

examples.ko: 입담만 믿고 준비 없이 나갔다가 말이 꼬였어요.
examples.en: I trusted my talking skills alone, went without preparing and got tongue-tied.

explain: '말솜씨'보다 이야기를 재미있고 맛깔나게 풀어 내는 재주라는 느낌이 강해요. '입담이 좋다/세다/걸쭉하다/구수하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with '말솜씨', it more strongly suggests a knack for telling stories in a fun, flavorful way. It is used like '입담이 좋다/세다/걸쭉하다/구수하다'.

examples.en: The event organizer greeted the participants.
The organizer prepared tents in case of rain.
Who is the organizer of this gathering?

examples.ko: 주최자 측에서 입장료를 받지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The organizers decided not to charge an entrance fee.
I sent an inquiry email to the tournament organizer.
He said he would take responsibility as the organizer.

explain: 행사 안내문에서 '주최'는 행사를 열고 책임지는 쪽, '주관'은 실제로 운영하는 쪽으로 나눠 쓰기도 해요. 진행을 맡은 사람은 '사회자'나 '진행자'이고, 파티를 여는 개인은 '호스트'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: On event notices, '주최' is the side that holds the event and takes responsibility, while '주관' is the side that actually runs it. The person emceeing is a '사회자' or '진행자', and a person throwing a party is more naturally a '호스트'.
